newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips firms drive Moroccan bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips firms drive Moroccan bourse lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its two-hour session lower on Wednesday, pulled down mainly by blue chip companies, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 434.95 points, down 0.36 percent over the previous session, a bourse official said.
"The bourse index was pulled down for the third consecutive day by the market's largest firms including ONA Group," a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, lost two dirhams to close at 480 dirhams.
Wafabank, one of the market's liquid stocks, lost five dirhams to close at 535 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a market blue chip, lost three dirhams to close at 400 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, remained stable at 687 dirhams.

Morocco has reduced the number of listed companies on the Casablanca bourse to 46 after it delisted Omnium Marocain d'Investissement firm (OMI), an official said. Traded volume on the official market was 30.2 million dirhams compared with 23.3 million dirhams on Tuesday. ($1= 8.6 dirhams)
